text:
Maya T: Hi team, day 2 and hitting a weird one. I can list namespaces and get svc objects but when I try to describe kube-proxy DaemonSet in kube-system I get Forbidden. Command: `kubectl -n kube-system describe daemonset kube-proxy`. Anyone know who to ping or what permission I should ask for?

Devon R: welcome Maya :wave: Typically describe on cluster/system DaemonSets requires that your user has permission on daemonsets in kube-system (namespaced). Run `kubectl auth can-i describe daemonsets -n kube-system`. Also check if you accidentally switched to a read-only serviceaccount.

Maya T: `kubectl auth can-i describe daemonsets -n kube-system` -> no. But `kubectl get svc -A` works. My kubeconfig has multiple contexts/users and I keep toggling.

Devon R: Get a minimal kubeconfig for the cluster you're working on:`kubectl config view --minify --flatten > /tmp/kube-maya` then `export KUBECONFIG=/tmp/kube-maya`. That will help avoid the wrong user entry being used.

Maya T: did that, switched to the flattened one, re-ran `auth can-i` and still no.

Devon R: Ok. For cluster-level view actions (like reading kube-system daemonsets) infra strongly prefers issuing timeboxed RoleBindings bound to your user email rather than giving SA tokens. File an INF ticket and request `get,list,watch,describe` on daemonsets in kube-system for 2 hours and they can apply it.

infra-bot: Reminder: do not request cluster-admin. Include justification, exact resources/verbs, and duration in the INF ticket. All temporary grants are logged.

Maya T: Curious: could impersonation help here for debugging (e.g., `kubectl --as=system:serviceaccount:kube-system:kube-proxy`)? I read about it but not sure if allowed.

Devon R: Impersonation (`--as`) is powerful but requires your account to have `impersonate` permission for that target identity. Infra doesn't grant impersonation widely. It's useful for debugging if infra temporarily grants it, but usually easier to request a timeboxed RoleBinding.

Maya T: One more odd thing: I tried creating a namespaced rolebinding in my team namespace to view cluster-level resources and infra bot yelled at me. Why can't a namespaced RoleBinding grant access to kube-system daemonsets?

Devon R: Namespaced RoleBindings only bind Role (namespaced) or ClusterRole to subjects for that namespace scope. To grant access to kube-system resources you need either a RoleBinding in kube-system that references a Role/ClusterRole or a ClusterRoleBinding (broad). So create the RoleBinding in kube-system and ask infra to apply it.

Onboard Bot: Pro tip: for first-week tasks we typically request the `view` ClusterRole on a per-namespace RoleBinding for team namespaces and a separate timeboxed cluster-level role for infra debugging. Check the onboarding doc: https://intra.redwood.dev/onboard/k8s-access

Maya T: Filed INF-1678 requesting a 3-hour RoleBinding in kube-system scoped to `get,list,watch,describe` for daemonsets for maya@redwood.com and attached logs of the failing commands.

Devon R: Nice. Once infra applies it, you can revert to your normal kubeconfig. If you want to keep things tidy for local dev, I recommend adding aliases in your shell: `alias kteam="KUBECONFIG=~/.kube/config-team && kubectl"`.

Maya T: Thanks all, the ticket got approved and infra applied a RoleBinding in kube-system. `kubectl -n kube-system describe daemonset kube-proxy` works now. Appreciate the quick help :tada:

Devon R: Welcome aboard and glad that fixed it. If you plan on running diagnostics often, infra can give you a small script that mints a temporary kubeconfig for the duration of the ticket. PM me if you want the script.

Maya T: Will do, thanks!
